questions.q: 10 supplier calls of 0.2 s each, mostly waiting for the network. One by one they take 2.0 s. With 10 threads?
questions.explain: Waiting doesn't need the CPU. While one thread waits, the others wait too, at the same time. The lab measured 0.2 s.

questions.q: Why didn't 4 threads speed up counting primes?
options: The GIL lets only one thread run Python code at a time, so computing threads just take turns
Primes can't be counted in parallel
The CPU had only one core
questions.explain: Threads help with waiting work, not computing work, in normal Python. The lab: one by one 1.3 s, 4 threads 1.3 s.

questions.q: What speeds up CPU-heavy work like counting primes?
options: Processes: separate Pythons, each with its own GIL, on its own CPU core
questions.explain: The lab: 4 processes took 0.5 s instead of 1.3 s on an 8-core machine.

questions.q: 5 threads try to buy the last pair of earbuds at once, without a lock. What can happen?
options: All 5 check 'stock > 0?' before any of them takes one, so 5 are sold and stock becomes -4
questions.explain: A race condition. with lock: around the check-and-take lets only one thread in at a time.

questions.q: The program starts 5 threads with t.start() and immediately prints len(prices): 0. What's missing?
options: t.join() for each thread, so the program waits until they finish
questions.explain: start() doesn't wait. join() does. A ThreadPoolExecutor in a with block joins for you.

questions.q: Which job should use threads rather than processes?
options: Computing a big sales report in pure Python
questions.explain: API calls are mostly waiting (I/O-bound): threads (or asyncio). The others are CPU-bound: processes.

questions.q: (Going deeper) pool.map(lambda p: p // 100, prices) in a ProcessPoolExecutor fails with PicklingError. Why?
options: Work is sent to another process by pickling it, and a lambda has no name to be found by
questions.explain: Use a named function defined at the top level of the file. Threads don't need pickling: they share memory.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What is Python 3.13's free-threaded build?
options: An experimental Python without the GIL, where threads can compute on several cores at once
questions.explain: Usually run as python3.13t. Still experimental; the lab's normal Python reports sys._is_gil_enabled() == True.
